title: Design canvas
description: A set of designs, each a frame on the canvas. Frames are laid out in rows, one row per group, in the order given.

context.description: Markdown shown above the canvas: what the designs are for and what to look at.

flow.description: Draws an arrow from each frame to the next one in its group, for the steps of a flow such as a wizard.

variants.description: The groups are alternatives, such as three designs of one dialog: the person can star one as the favorite.

frames.description: The designs. Ids must be unique; a frame whose id repeats an earlier one is left out.

id.description: Stable across rounds, so the next round can show what was said about the same frame.

group.description: The row the frame goes in, under this caption: a variant, a theme or a part of the flow. Frames without one share a row.

notes.description: Markdown: what this frame shows, or what to decide about it.

width.description: The frame's width in CSS pixels. An HTML frame defaults to 1280; an image, to its own width.

height.description: The frame's height in CSS pixels. Without it, the frame is as tall as its content.

html.description: A whole, self-contained HTML document: styles in <style> elements, images and fonts as data URIs. Scripts do not run, and links and forms go nowhere.

file.description: The HTML document as an .html file sent with --attach, in place of `html`.

image.description: A PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or SVG image sent with --attach, in place of `html`.
